Question 4 of 11 · Is there a Creator?

One Creator or many?

Why the unity of natural law points to a single source.

The case

01

Could there be multiple creators rather than one?

The universe operates under one consistent set of physical laws — everywhere, at all times.

The argument for one Creator

Multiple competing creators would logically produce inconsistency and conflict. The unity of natural law — gravity works the same everywhere, light travels at the same speed — points to a single unified source.

Read more

This is the Argument from Unity. If two gods disagreed on the laws of physics, the universe would be chaotic. Its remarkable consistency points to one will behind it.

02

You believe in multiple gods. The universe operates under one unified set of physical laws — everywhere, at all times. Does that suggest one source or many?

Gravity works the same on the moon as it does on Earth. Light travels at the same speed everywhere.

Objections, answered

The strongest pushback we hear, and our answer to each.

You might say“Multiple creators is possible”

Our answer

Multiple creators produce a logical problem.

The problem with multiple gods

If multiple creators existed with equal power, any decision one made could be overruled by another. Nothing would be stable. Yet the universe has precise, unvarying laws — strong evidence of a single will.

You might say“The gods could agree on the laws”

Our answer

If gods agree — what makes them gods?

The problem with agreeing gods

If multiple gods must agree and defer to each other, none is truly all-powerful or independent. You'd need a higher principle governing them all — which is, effectively, the one God.
